acceptance.criterion: docs/algorithm.md specifies the fixed argument, the model row, the free-only symmetry rows, the post-solve check, the error table, turf_min_cover and turf_sizes with fixed, and the fixed result field.
conformance/generate.py --check passes and test_generate.py passes, with fixed cases for turf, min_cover, and sizes that cover every required case in the design.
The expected values of the fixed cases come from exact enumeration over portfolios that contain every fixed product.
R turf(), turf_min_cover(), and turf_sizes() accept fixed and pass every conformance fixture with Rscript conformance/run_r.R, and run_r.R loads the fixed cases and passes fixed into each call.
testthat covers each new error message and the case of a fixed product that is the later twin of a free product, and R CMD check gives no new NOTE, WARNING, or ERROR.
Calls without fixed give the same results as before (existing tests and fixtures pass unchanged).
print() of a portfolio with fixed products shows a Fixed: line with the product names, and no such line without them.

Python turf, turf_min_cover, and turf_sizes accept keyword-only fixed and pytest passes, conformance included, with presolve on and off, and the Python runner loads the fixed cases and passes fixed into each call.

JavaScript turf, turfMinCover, and turfSizes accept options.fixed, and npm run typecheck, test, build, and test:conformance pass, with presolve on and off, and the JavaScript runner loads the fixed cases and passes fixed into each call.
Each port tests each new error message with the exact text and error type.
The dashboard settings let the user fix products, and a run returns portfolios that contain them for every size, with the smallest size at the number of fixed products.
The stage counts, the trade-off, the contributions chart, the table, and the CSV use the fixed products of the run.

npm run typecheck, test, build, and test:browser pass in dashboard/, with a test for a fixed run, fixed stage counts, and a fixed trade-off that ends complete with maxFrequency equal to the fixed reaches plus the largest free reaches.
Loading another data set clears the fixed products, and a threshold change unfixes only the products whose reach becomes zero and says so on the page.
README.md, python/README.md, js/README.md, dashboard/README.md, roxygen and man/, and NEWS.md describe fixed products.

R, Python, JavaScript, and dashboard versions are 0.3.0 in every file that carries the version, lock files (python/uv.lock, js and dashboard package-lock.json), python/src/turflp/__init__.py, and README examples included.

Every GitHub Actions check on the exact final PR head is green, the Python wheel and Next.js example checks included.
The PR is merged with a merge commit, release v0.3.0 is published on that merge commit with turflp-dashboard.html attached, and the publish-npm and publish-python workflows of the release succeed.
